docs-claims-d022a56f2.text:
`InferenceIncidKKNewcombeRiskDiff` (3):
  - “If a design has no matched pairs or no reservoir subjects, the single available component is used directly” (R/EDI/R/inference_incidence_KK_newcombe_ivwc_univ.R:20; partly tested): Only the reservoir-only case (m == 0) is tested. The matched-pairs-only case (no reservoir subjects, or one reservoir arm empty: pool_estimates_ivwc's ok1-only branch at :106-107) has no test.; nearest test: R/package_tests/testthat_bulk/test-kk-newcombe-ivwc-compound-reference.R:69; test idea: Use a KK fixture (or injected KKstats) with nRT == 0 or nRC == 0 and check that the estimate equals (d_plus - d_minus)/m and the SE equals sqrt of the paired variance.
  - “initialize requires an incidence response and a KK matching-on-the-fly design” (R/EDI/R/inference_incidence_KK_newcombe_ivwc_univ.R:44; no test); nearest test: R/package_tests/testthat_bulk/test-kk-newcombe-ivwc-no-match-structure-and-neither-component-usable-guards-reference.R:33 (injects has_match_structure = FALSE after construction; bypasses the initialize guard); test idea: Check that InferenceIncidKKNewcombeRiskDiff$new() errors with 'requires a KK matching-on-the-fly design' on a non-KK incidence design, and errors on a KK continuous design.
  - “Matched-pair component applies the paired Newcombe (Method-10-style Wilson-score) interval; reservoir component applies the independent-samples Newcombe interval” (R/EDI/R/inference_incidence_KK_newcombe_ivwc_univ.R:9; a test or the code contradicts it): Neither component uses a Wilson-score interval. shared_combined() uses the plain Wald paired-difference variance (p10 + p01 - (p10 - p01)^2)/m (R/EDI/R/inference_incidence_KK_newcombe_ivwc_univ.R:147) and the Wald two-sample variance pRT(1-pRT)/nRT + pRC(1-pRC)/nRC (:157). The reference test pins exactly those Wald formulas (test-kk-newcombe-ivwc-compound-reference.R:33,39), so the documented Newcombe/Wilson behaviour has no implementation and no test.; nearest test: R/package_tests/testthat_bulk/test-kk-newcombe-ivwc-compound-reference.R:24-39; test idea: Compare each component's variance or CI with a hand-computed Newcombe Method-10 (paired) and Method-10 (independent) Wilson-score interval on a small fixed table, or change the docs to say Wald.

`InferenceCountZeroInflatedNegBin` (3):
  - “Jackknife inference is not supported: compute_jackknife_estimate() and related methods report explicit non-estimability” (R/EDI/R/inference_count_zero_inflated.R:280; partly tested): The jackknife refusal is inherited from the shared abstract, but the only refusal test builds a ZIP object (line 20). The ZINB pass of test-count-likelihood-families-focused.R:225-233 tolerates either outcome and does not assert the refusal.; nearest test: R/package_tests/testthat_bulk/test-zero-augmented-poisson-jackknife-refusal-and-bca-type-guard-reference.R:28 (InferenceCountZeroInflatedPoisson only); test idea: For InferenceCountZeroInflatedNegBin, call each compute_jackknife_* method and expect NA together with the 'zero_augmented_poisson_jackknife_not_supported' reason.
  - “Inside resampling (nonparametric, Bayesian or parametric bootstrap) a zero-free replicate falls back to the non-inflated negative binomial fit” (R/EDI/R/inference_count_zero_inflated.R:291; partly tested): Only the nonparametric bootstrap worker is exercised. The Bayesian-bootstrap weighted refit and the parametric-bootstrap simulation fallbacks have no ZINB test.; nearest test: R/package_tests/testthat_bulk/test-zero-inflated-no-zeros-error-and-resampling-fallback.R:42 'ZINB bootstrap replicate with no zeros gets the negative binomial fit'; test idea: For ZINB, call compute_estimate_with_bootstrap_weights with zero weight on all zero-response rows and expect a finite estimate matching an NB/Poisson fit on the remaining rows.
  - “compute_estimate: under estimand = 'marginal_mean_diff' or 'marginal_ratio' (set via set_estimand()), returns the g-computation marginal mean difference or log-scale marginal ratio” (R/EDI/R/inference_count_zero_inflated.R:350; a test or the code contradicts it): The method doc says ZINB supports the marginal estimands. The class doc (inference_count_zero_inflated.R:273-275) and the test at test-zip-hurdle-poisson-marginal-estimand.R:207 (expect_false(inf_zinb$supports('marginal_estimand'))) both say it does not. ZINB is a plain R6 class that does not compose MarginalEstimand (inference_count_zero_inflated.R:326), so the marginal branch is dead code and the method doc is wrong.; nearest test: R/EDI/tests/testthat/test-zip-hurdle-poisson-marginal-estimand.R:203 'NegBin siblings do not support a marginal estimand'; test idea: Assert that set_estimand('marginal_mean_diff') errors on InferenceCountZeroInflatedNegBin, pinning the class-level claim; separately, correct the compute_estimate description.

docs-claims-d42892ef3.text:
`InferenceIncidExactZhang` (2):
  - “Point estimate is the Haldane-Anscombe log OR from the pooled 2x2 table across all subjects (matched and reservoir together)” (R/EDI/R/inference_incidence_exact_zhang.R:119; a test or the code contradicts it): On KK designs, zhang_get_exact_stats() returns n11/n10/n01/n00 counted over reservoir subjects only (test :52 'KK statistics ... reservoir 2x2 counts'), and compute_estimate() (inference_incidence_exact_zhang.R:24-26) is the HA log OR of those stats (test :84). R/EDI/tests/testthat/test-zhang-exact-ci-inverts-combined-test.R:5 also notes that the reservoir-only log OR is always 0 when every subject is matched. So the estimate uses the reservoir table, not a table pooled over all subjects. The same claim appears in man-roxygen/exact-zhang-compute-estimate.R:1-5.; nearest test: R/package_tests/testthat_bulk/test-zhang-exact-incidence-stats-pvalues-and-ci-search-reference.R:84 'closed-form estimate (0.5-corrected log odds ratio) and Wald interval'; test idea: On a KK design with both matched pairs and a reservoir, compare compute_estimate() with the HA log OR of the 2x2 table pooled over all subjects (or, if the reservoir-only behaviour is intended, fix the docs).
  - “Requires an uncensored incidence response” (R/EDI/man-roxygen/exact-zhang-initialize.R:3; no test); test idea: Build a Bernoulli design with a continuous response and expect InferenceIncidExactZhang$new() to error.
